text: But understand this: in the last days there will come times of hardship.
For people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
heartless, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, with no love for good,
treacherous, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God—
holding to the outward form of godliness but denying its power. Keep away from such people.

take captive weak-willed women, loaded down with sins and driven by all kinds of desires,[^1]

[^1]: The Greek word rendered *weak-willed women* is a diminutive form suggesting vulnerable or gullible women; it describes those targeted by the false teachers, not women in general.

versions.text: For among them are those who worm their way into households and take captive weak-willed women, loaded down with sins and driven by all kinds of desires,
versions.explanation: γυναικάρια is a diminutive that can sound demeaning in English without explanation; a brief footnote clarifies the sense and guards against a misapplied generalization.

text: always learning yet never able to arrive at a knowledge of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these men also oppose the truth—men of corrupted minds, who fail the test when it comes to the faith.
But they will not get far, for their folly will be plain to everyone, just as the folly of those two men was.

versions.text: But they will not get far, for their folly will be plain to everyone, as theirs also was.
versions.explanation: The pronoun ἐκείνων points back to Jannes and Jambres, but in English "as theirs also was" is ambiguous, since "their folly" was just used of the opponents. Naming the referent removes the confusion, especially when read aloud.

text: You, however, have followed closely my teaching, my way of life, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my endurance,
my persecutions and sufferings—what happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra, the kinds of persecutions I endured. And the Lord rescued me from them all.
Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted,
while evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it,
and how from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, for rebuking, for correcting, and for training in righteousness,
so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
